levels.0: Lists 'upload and watch' only, or drifts into recommendations, comments and live streaming unasked.
levels.1: Covers upload, transcoding and playback, but treats view counts or resumable uploads as an afterthought, or never says live is out of scope.
levels.2: Covers resumable upload, transcoding into a ladder, adaptive playback, video pages and deduplicated view counts; puts live, search, recommendations and DRM explicitly out of scope; names the write side (batch) and read side (bandwidth) as different problems.

levels.0: No latency, rebuffering or durability targets.
levels.1: States a start-up time and availability, but not rebuffering, upload-to-watchable time or when an upload counts as durable.
levels.2: Start-up under 2 s, rebuffering well under 1% of watch time, first rendition within minutes, 99.99% playback vs 99.9% upload availability, and an acknowledged upload never lost; counting never on the playback path.

levels.0: No numbers, or numbers without derivation.
levels.1: Derives concurrency or egress but not both, or no peak.
levels.2: 200M viewer-hours ÷ 24 = 8.33M concurrent; × 3 Mbps = 25 Tbps (50 Tbps peak, 270 PB/day); 6 s segments → 1.39M requests/s; 13,889 plays/s; 152,778 events/s; concludes the CDN is the main design driver.

levels.1: Computes uploads per second or storage, but not encoding compute.
levels.2: 500 h/min = 30,000 s of video per second, 50 videos/s, 3.24 PB/day of originals plus ~3.4 PB of renditions, and an encoding fleet derived from an explicit CPU-seconds-per-second assumption (about 120,000 vCPUs).

levels.0: A single upload endpoint that receives the file, and a 'stream' endpoint.
levels.1: Presigned uploads and a play endpoint, but no resume, no completion step or no event batching.
levels.2: Upload session with idempotency key, presigned part URLs in batches, resume by listing parts, complete → 202 processing; play-info returning signed manifest URLs (with a fallback CDN); a manifest example; batched 202 event endpoint.

criteria.title: Metadata, pipeline state and object layout

levels.0: Stores videos 'in the database' with no separation of bytes and metadata.
levels.1: Separates object storage from metadata but has no place for job state or picks a store without a reason.
levels.2: Video and channel tables keyed for their access patterns, transactional pipeline state (or a workflow engine), deterministic object keys that make retries safe, a separate counter store, and a store choice justified by access pattern and operations (Vitess-style sharded MySQL named as valid).

levels.0: A box diagram with servers streaming video from a database.
levels.1: Shows upload to storage, a transcoder and a CDN, but no walkthrough of play start or events.
levels.2: Walks upload, transcode, publish, play start (cache-aside play-info, signed URL, then CDN only) and events separately, with a start-up latency budget under 2 s and zone-redundant API tiers.

criteria.title: Resumable uploads and the transcoding DAG

levels.0: Proxies uploads through the API and transcodes each video as one job.
levels.1: Uses presigned multipart uploads and parallel encoding, but without leases, idempotent retries or failure handling.
levels.2: Multipart with part checksums and lifecycle cleanup; a DAG of probe, per-chunk-per-rendition encodes, packaging and publish; leases, deterministic outputs, dead-letter queue for poison videos, priority lanes so first renditions stay fast.

levels.0: Serves a single MP4 file per resolution chosen by the server.
levels.1: Knows HLS/DASH and the player switching quality, but cannot justify segment length or the ladder.
levels.2: Player-driven ABR (throughput vs buffer-based), a concrete ladder with bitrates, 6 s segments justified by request count vs switching speed, CMAF serving both HLS and DASH, and per-title or popularity-based codec choice.

criteria.title: CDN tiers, long tail and hot releases

levels.0: 'Put a CDN in front' with no hit rates or origin sizing.
levels.1: Has edge caching and a hit rate, but no shield, no plan for the long tail or a hot release.
levels.2: Edge + shield + origin with origin load derived (about 1% of requests), cache keys without signatures, immutable segments vs short-TTL manifests, request coalescing, pre-positioning, multi-CDN fallback, and a PoP-failure timeline.

criteria.title: View counting at 300,000 events per second

levels.0: Increments a counter row per play.
levels.1: Sends events asynchronously but has no definition of a view, no deduplication or no replay safety.
levels.2: Collectors → Kafka → aggregators partitioned by video, a stated view rule, per-session dedup, batched flushes with idempotent replay, hot videos as busy threads not hot rows, and a batch fraud-correction pass.

levels.1: Covers server and zone loss but not CDN, origin, poison uploads or what breaks first at 10×.
levels.2: Zone loss with N+1 sizing, PoP failure, origin overload, cache loss, poison uploads, takedowns; at 10× names egress first, then encoding cost (hardware encoders, lazy rungs) and storage tiering.

levels.1: Generic trade-offs not tied to this design.
levels.2: Each key choice (direct uploads, chunk length, segment length, codec policy, CDN tiers, zone-local event buffers, streaming aggregation) comes with the alternative and the reason it lost here.
